cases.customer_question: When creating a derivative product from an already qualified product, is additional Bluetooth qualification testing required?
question_variants: Can a product variant be added without new qualification testing?
How is a Bluetooth derivative product registered?
Is additional registration sufficient for a product variant?
Can qualification be reused when Bluetooth technology is unchanged?
cases.actual_issue: Determining whether a derivative product can reuse an existing Bluetooth qualification when the Bluetooth implementation has not changed.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The customer asked about launching a product variant based on a previously qualified design. The consultant explained that if the Bluetooth technology implementation remains unchanged, new qualification testing is not required. Instead, the product can be added through an additional registration process.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant stated that when there is no change to the Bluetooth technology implementation, including the Bluetooth module and related Bluetooth functionality, qualification testing is unnecessary. The product may be handled through an additional registration process rather than repeating qualification testing.
cases.decision_logic: The deciding factor is whether the Bluetooth implementation has changed. If the Bluetooth technology remains unchanged from the previously qualified product, qualification reuse is permitted and new testing is not required.
cases.final_recommendation: Confirm that the Bluetooth implementation is unchanged and then use the applicable additional-registration process instead of initiating a new qualification test campaign.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Performing unnecessary requalification can create avoidable cost and effort. Reusing a qualification without verifying that the Bluetooth implementation is unchanged could result in an incorrect registration approach.
